goal: one user action equals one document transaction
positive_oracle: One UI action creates one transaction and one revision even with multiple objects
negative_oracle: Mid-operation failure rolls back every change and preserves undo journal
method: git rev-parse HEAD + git status in the pinned checkout, then bounded file reads with line numbers. Decisions are OM9-owned; no upstream code is copied.

observed_symbols: gui.rs:354 comment: THE ONE DOORWAY OF THE FEATURE TREE / gui.rs:448 comment: carry out what the properties panel asked for, after it has drawn
planned_anchors.what_is_missing: the command applies its change in one place, after the user has finished choosing. QymCAD has no transaction object at all: a change is applied directly, so a failure halfway cannot be taken back.

implemented_api_before_this_task: session.rs::accept_world_point builds ONE TransactionRequest for the finished command and calls coordinator.prepare_with_held_usage then commit; the session state advances only on receipt.published
TransactionCoordinator::commit returns a Receipt { published } and the undo journal counts the published transactions
gap_found_by_this_task: Pinned rather than changed: one completed command adds exactly one journal entry and exactly one entity; a command refused at any step (zero length, Busy, stale context, Escape) adds none and moves no entity count. The probe behind these fixtures showed context_revision does NOT move on an edit — it is the document identity token — so the per-action counter the plan means is the journal/epoch, and the api.md says so instead of pretending otherwise.

The all-or-nothing property of a multi-mutation request is the coordinator's own contract (`cargo test -p om9-core` in the evidence log); the fixtures pin what the session adds on top: exactly one request per finished command.
reuse_decision: ADAPT the single doorway of gui.rs (apply once, at the end); ADD the prepared/committed transaction and the journal.
